name: Archer-Daniels-Midland
description: ADM buys crops (soybeans, corn, wheat and others) from farmers and grain elevators around the world, stores and ships them, and turns them into oils, protein meal, sweeteners, starches, ethanol, food ingredients and animal feed. Most of its $80B of revenue is pass-through commodity value; the profit is the small spread between what it pays for crops and what it sells the products for, plus fees for storage, logistics and trading. Profit swings with crush margins (the price of oil and meal minus the beans), ethanol and biofuel policy, and crop size and trade flows. FY2025 total segment operating profit fell 23% to $3.2B because crush margins compressed; the first half of 2026 recovered to $2.2B from $1.6B a year earlier. It also owns 22.5% of Singapore-listed Wilmar, whose earnings it books inside its Ag Services and Oilseeds segment.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source. SEC SIC code is 2070 (Fats & Oils) per the EDGAR submissions record. Mowgli classification is not set here.

hq.note: 77 W. Wacker Dr., Chicago, IL 60601 (EDGAR business address); incorporated in Delaware

employees.note: FY2025 10-K table: 18,851 North America, 9,528 Latin America, 10,202 EMEA, 2,915 APAC

businessLines.name: Ag Services and Oilseeds
businessLines.how: Customers (food, feed, energy and industrial buyers, renewable diesel makers, other traders) pay a commodity price per tonne for grain, meal and oil; ADM keeps the margin between crop cost and product price plus fees for handling and storage. Profit is driven by the crush margin, trade flows and biofuel policy, not by revenue, which mostly reflects commodity prices.
businessLines.description: Grain origination, merchandising, transport and storage; crushing of soybeans and other oilseeds into oil and meal; refined oils and biodiesel; 22.5% share of Wilmar.

businessLines.name: Carbohydrate Solutions
businessLines.how: Food, beverage and industrial customers buy sweeteners and starches under contracts or spot; fuel blenders buy ethanol at market prices. ADM earns the spread between corn cost and product prices; the Vantage ethanol unit is much more exposed to ethanol margins.
businessLines.description: Corn and wheat wet and dry milling: sweeteners, starches, syrups, flour, dextrose, ethanol (via Vantage Corn Processors) and distillers' grains.

businessLines.name: Nutrition
businessLines.how: Food, beverage, supplement, feed and pet-food makers buy specialty ingredients and blends, typically repeat orders priced per product rather than at a commodity index, so margins are steadier and higher than in crushing.
businessLines.description: Human Nutrition (flavors, colors, plant proteins, emulsifiers, fibers, probiotics, botanical extracts) and Animal Nutrition (feed, premix, additives, pet food).

businessLines.name: Other Business
businessLines.how: Futures brokerage commissions and clearing fees from customers, plus premiums retained by ADM's own captive insurer.
businessLines.description: ADM Investor Services (futures commission merchant) and a captive insurance business. Not a reportable segment.

brands.note: Singapore-listed agribusiness (palm, oilseeds crushing, edible oils, sugar, fertilizer). Equity method.
